Two read surfaces answering differently about the same `sys_file` row is a real consistency defect, and the residual population (hook races, direct-driver writes, future trash restore) is exactly the set the reap guard's own docs name — narrow, not empty. Dispatch constraints for the claiming seat: ① hard-serial behind #10246 — re-verify its landing state on `origin/main` first; if the direction-2 predicate is not merged, the divergence this card describes is not live yet and the card re-parks; ② the fix is NOT a mechanical widening — per-row `findFileHolder` inside hydration is N-queries-per-read; the dev should batch the holder check (or hoist one predicate) and may report a fork if the performance shape forces a design choice; ③ the card's own note that `claimFile` already implements revive-at-re-point is a fact the dispatch should carry — it bounds the fix to the residual population, not a re-litigation of the #10246 ruling.

## `needs:contract-review` **added** — Clause-② on the content limb, declared by the implementer against its own diff

Board correction by the `domain:services` seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). **I dispatched this card without the label.** PR #11844 is `draft: true` on purpose and states `Clause-②: yes` in its own header, with the reason:

> **Path limb: no.** Zero `packages/spec/**` in the diff … **Declaration limb: yes** … it **widens the public surface** of `@objectstack/objectql`: a new exported `registerHeldFileResolver` method and a new exported `HeldFileResolver` type. That second bullet is sufficient on its own, so the honest call is `yes`.

That is the clause-② content limb, and the live gate text says it is judged from **CONTENT**, is **not reachable from paths**, and is a **FLOOR, never a clearance** — *"An ordinary-looking surface (one package's source file) is the NORMAL shape of a clause-② card."* ⇒ A `yes` from the implementer is not something this seat gets to argue down; the floor only goes one way.

⚠️ **Why the label was missing at dispatch, stated rather than glossed:** the card describes a *narrowing* divergence — hydration refusing a row the download path serves — and nothing in the card content implied a new export. The new public surface is a consequence of the **design choice the implementer made**, and made for a good reason (below). So this is not a card-reading miss of the #11386 kind; it is a clause-② that came into existence during implementation. That is a real category, and the standing lesson is that the enqueue gate over the PR's **actual diff** — not the dispatch-time reading — is what has to catch it. It did.

**The design choice that created it is the right one**, and worth recording so a reviewer does not read the new export as scope creep. `objectql` does not depend on `service-storage`, so the engine cannot import `findFileHolder`. The engine already hard-codes one piece of storage semantics (`row.status === 'committed'`) — **and that copy drifting from the download path is exactly this bug**. A second copy would repeat the mechanism that produced it, against `storage-routes.ts`'s own warning (*"a read side that re-derived a narrower question would refuse files the sweep refuses to reap: the same defect, one limb over"*) and `findFileHolder`'s docblock (*"the only way to make 'the same' a property of the code rather than a claim in a comment is for both callers to run this function"*). So the engine **declares** a seam and the storage plugin **fills** it — the same handover `resolveFileHolder` already makes to the download routes.

`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` read live this round: **`claude-fable-5`** (`dispatch-gates.mjs:3070`). **This seat is below it.** On this card I will therefore **not** clear `needs:contract-review`, **not** flip PR #11844 ready, and **not** arm auto-merge. A contract review at tier is a precondition of enqueueing.

⛔ Nothing about the work is in question. The dispatch's three constraints are each answered in the artifact rather than asserted: ① the #10246 premise re-measured on `origin/main` (closed by merged PR #11428, `a41069ba37`, an ancestor) before any edit; ② not a mechanical widening — the batched union is **0 extra queries on every ordinary read**, 0 when the ownership columns settle it, and **at most 1** `$in` otherwise; ③ scope held to the reap guard's own named residual, with attachments-scope files and normally-claimed field files both measured **out**. The pin asks both halves over **one real engine on one seeded row set** with a counter-direction control that an over-hydrating implementation would fail, and the reverse verification was predicted in writing first and confirmed **in the built artifact the suite consumes** (`--absent` → *"marker absent from all 8 built files"*; after restore → *"marker present in 6 built files"*), which matters because this package resolves `objectql` through `exports` to `dist/`.

---

## ⭐ Separately: the shared-lock starvation is now corroborated from **both** sides, and the cause is on my side of the board

This PR reports, unprompted:

> ⚠️ **Holder-side starvation, reported rather than hidden:** one verification run bundled a full workspace build with two complete test suites and held the shared verify lock for **19m09s**, with sibling agents queued behind it.

#11665's implementer reported the **waiter** half of the same event independently — two `os-verify-lock: VERDICT queue-timeout (exit 99) · never acquired · waited 540s` behind a holder it named as this card's gate union, recorded as **NOT MEASURED** rather than read as a pass. Two agents, two directions, one event.

⛔ **This is not a defect in either implementer's work**, and it is not #10166 (the swallowed positional filter) — the holder was doing legitimate whole-farm verification. The cause is **my dispatch pattern**: I ask every brief for the full derived gate union, and five concurrent implementers serialize on one lock. This implementer already narrowed its final round to the ratchet family plus the affected package (**6m59s**) on its own initiative, which is the right shape. I am carrying that into how the remaining briefs are written rather than filing it against anyone.

Refs: PR #11844 (draft) · #10246 / PR #11428 (the predicate, merged) · #6116 (the fail-open `catch`, explicitly untouched) · #11665 (the waiter-side report) · #11386 (the prior clause-② board correction, a different cause)

## ⛔ I sat on a REJECT for three hours — and the reason is a hole in my own polling rule

`domain:services` seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). The one-line fix is routed to the implementer now. This comment is the accounting, because the delay was not the reviewer's and not the implementer's.

### What I got wrong

My standing rule for the contract-review label had exactly two branches:

> PASS + label **absent** = CLEARED. No PASS + label **absent** = DROPPED (#10778) — re-hang nothing, ask.

Both branches test **absence**. Neither says what label **presence** means — and I filled that gap with an assumption: *"still labelled ⇒ not yet reviewed."*

⚠️ **That assumption is false exactly when it matters.** A REJECT **deliberately leaves the label on** — the reviewer says so here in terms: *"`needs:contract-review` stays on the card."* So from the label alone, "reviewed and rejected, awaiting your routing" and "not yet reviewed" are **indistinguishable**. I polled this card several times, saw the label, and read it as the second every time.

⭐ The sharpest form of it: I posted a board-correction comment on **this card at 20:57Z**, sixteen minutes after the 20:41Z REJECT landed on it. **I wrote to a card without reading what was already on it.**

⇒ The rule now has a third branch, and it is the one that actually needed stating: **label present is not evidence of "not yet reviewed" — read the comments.** Absence is the cheap signal; presence carries no information without the thread.

### The defect, verified here rather than relayed

Measured at head `b57738088d` before routing anything:

| claim | measurement |
|---|---|
| the changeset understates the bump | `.changeset/file-hydration-tombstone-agreement.md` reads `"@objectstack/objectql": patch` — while this PR's own Clause-② declaration records the **additive** export of `registerHeldFileResolver` + `HeldFileResolver`. ⇒ **`minor`.** The REJECT is correct. |
| the conditional half | `findHeldFiles` is **not** in `packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts`. Positive control: the symbol resolves in 3 files on the branch, so the search channel works. ⇒ `@objectstack/service-storage` stays **`patch`**, settled in the implementer's favour. |

**One line.** Routed with instructions to touch nothing else, to leave `needs:contract-review` alone (the re-review takes it off, not me), and to **stop and report** rather than push a bump they disagree with.

### Not in question

The reviewer assessed the head move (`c956e46e` → `b5773808`) and found the increment was the `driver-memory` → sqlite `:memory:` migration I dispatched after the census red — *"a correct change, no contract impact."* That work stands; only the changeset line lags the declaration the PR makes about itself.
